claims.claim: Malformed PackageReference, ProjectReference or PackageVersion start-tag attributes produce a manifest-check error rather than being silently skipped.
claims.trigger: A recognized manifest element has unclosed/mismatched attribute quotes or an unquoted attribute value
claims.exceptions: Only the specific XML start-tag parser acceptance checks are established; this is not complete XML validation.
claims.enforcement_effect: Adds an error; CLI exits 1 when errors exist (lines 295..298); post-change handling reviewed separately.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Both describe malformed-element errors but dismiss the range as implementation without a separately registered constraint.
Version placement and inactive/commented XML evaluation do not express the malformed-attribute error condition.

claims.comparison_reason: A malformed attribute can trigger failure even without a forbidden version or architectural edge; this is a separate effective acceptance condition.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A recognized PackageReference has an unquoted Include attribute but no version. It yields an error independently of CPM version-placement checks.

claims.claim: A manifest that cannot be read or decoded by the accepted UTF-8/BOM-tagged UTF-16 decoder produces a check error with a request to save readable encoding.
claims.trigger: An existing recognized manifest returns readText.error
claims.exceptions: A missing file returns no findings in checkFile itself; CLI missing-target checking is separate. Valid BOM-tagged UTF-16 is accepted despite UTF-8 formatting preference.
claims.enforcement_effect: Adds manifest error and returns before semantic checks; CLI aggregates errors and exits 1.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Formatting charset preferences do not specify manifest decoding errors or acceptance of BOM-tagged UTF-16.
Fail-closed pre-command input decoding has a different target and timing; helper decoding is classified implementation.

claims.comparison_reason: Unreadable manifest content fails validation before dependency semantics and has a different trigger and severity from editor formatting or hook input.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: A tracked package manifest contains malformed UTF-8 bytes but otherwise no forbidden dependency; checker records a manifest error without evaluating package content.

claims.claim: An explicitly targeted manifest under a contained directory whose name starts with two dots is rejected as outside the repository.
claims.trigger: Explicit target resolves to a relative path such as ..cache/package.json inside the root
claims.exceptions: Repository-wide scanning separately skips dot-directories; the hypothesis concerns explicit targets. Ordinary parent traversal is correctly rejected.
claims.enforcement_effect: rel.startsWith('..') records an outside-root error; repo.toRelative lines 60..63 has a similar prefix test, with hook effects pending full caller review.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Skipping dot-directories during scans and Git-root precedence do not register false rejection of an explicit contained target.

claims.comparison_reason: Lexical prefix rejection is stricter than actual parent traversal containment, but whether this accidental edge is a registrable effective constraint remains uncertain.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: The existing file root/..cache/package.json is supplied explicitly; its relative string starts with '..' and the CLI labels it outside root.
claims.open_question: Should this parser/path edge count as an effective constraint, and which hook paths also inherit it?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Inspect hook callers and use a pure path-function probe if needed in the actual-trigger sweep.

claims.claim: A PackageVersion missing its Version attribute skips both version validation and the package-name deny-list check.
claims.trigger: A readable PackageVersion has Include but no Version attribute
claims.exceptions: Other MSBuild tooling may reject the manifest; this concerns this checker's result only. Missing Include also skips the loop body.
claims.enforcement_effect: The continue at line 175 bypasses checkNugetName at line 181, even for a listed deprecated package.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Registered package-name errors are stated without this missing-Version exception.
The loop is implementation or linked to pinning; independent discusses mandatory local CPM and floating/range/property versions, not bypass of the deny-list through an omitted Version.

claims.comparison_reason: This exception changes whether a prohibited name is reported, independently of whether the version is pinned. Its normative relevance to a build-invalid form is unresolved.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Directory.Packages.props enables CPM and contains a readable PackageVersion Include='FluentValidation.AspNetCore' with no Version; this loop does not emit the deprecated-package error.
claims.open_question: Is omission-triggered non-enforcement on this manifest form relevant as an effective exception, or only invalid-input implementation behavior?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Pure copied-function probe and cross-check against declared checker obligations in the executable-enforcement pass.
